scope: Read-only local source/Git-object and retained-evidence review, plus official upstream source retrieval at one pinned revision. No device diagnostics, models, builds, process or power probes, CI actions or new measurement workload were executed by this reviewer.

metrics.timeToFirstToken: Receive timestamp of first eligible nonempty content token minus monotonic HTTP request start; model startup is excluded.
metrics.generationTokensPerSecond: (reported completion usage - 1) / (last eligible content-token receive time - first eligible content-token receive time)
metrics.boundary: Client-observed token delivery, including transport/backpressure and receive buffering; this is not isolated runtime/kernel decode TPS.
metrics.receiveBufferRule: Events completed in the same receive buffer share its observed timestamp; do not fabricate per-event interpolation. A nonpositive first-to-last interval is ineligible.
metrics.usageRule: Use terminal reported completion usage for the numerator. SSE event or byte counts do not by themselves establish generated-token counts.
metrics.streamRule: Parse each framed stream incrementally; role-only events, headers and terminal markers are not the first output token. Require successful terminal framing, usage and finish reason.

nativeRust.sourceContract: One generated-token callback feeds its vocabulary piece to the incremental UTF-8 display and emits at most one nonempty text delta. The server splits an individual delta only above its 1024-byte input chunk bound. Thinking-disabled output passes through as content. Each framed write is flushed. A final incomplete UTF-8 suffix would produce a non-ASCII replacement character.
eligibility: Thinking disabled; no reasoning or tool-call output.
Terminal reported completion usage is exactly the selected eight-token cap and finish reason is length.
There are exactly eight nonempty content deltas and their complete concatenation is ASCII and shorter than 1024 bytes.
The complete output is the fixed counting-prompt prefix; retain the individual pieces and receive timestamps.
The first-to-last content receive interval is positive.
nativeRust.inference: Under these conditions no byte-bound split or UTF-8 completion can add a content event. Equality between nonempty deltas and reported usage therefore establishes one visible delta per generated token for this restricted workload. This conclusion does not apply to arbitrary SSE streams.

publisherCpp.sourceContract: With speculation disabled the sampling path advances its generated-token count once and processes one token piece. Valid UTF-8 is forwarded through one partial result. Chat message differencing produces at most one content difference per parser update; the no-tool Qwen3.5 content parser consumes the remaining plain text without waiting for EOF. The final stream can separately emit remaining parser differences, so arbitrary event-count equality alone is insufficient.
publisherCpp.conditionalEligibility: Apply the native eight-token/ASCII/counting-output restrictions, require no reasoning, tools or stop-marker text, and use the supported no-tool plain-content parser. Treat other output as ineligible rather than assuming a one-token event mapping.
publisherCpp.backendSchemaScope: These are direct C++ backend controls. The broker-public enable_thinking and abliteration_scale keys require their documented backend translation; native Rust uses its own accepted request schema.
publisherCpp.retainedTimingFields: The final chat-stream event includes stats when available. Its predicted_n and predicted_ms are the server's generated count and generation milliseconds; preserve them as a separate observation, not an interchangeable client interval.
